request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 33.6% (95% band 23.9% to 47.7%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.6; >= 2: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.42, 95% band [+1.96, +2.57]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 21.4% (95% band 15.0% to 26.8%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 159999: +0.3; >= 160000: -0.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.14, 95% band [-1.77, -0.66]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 9.9% (95% band 3.8% to 14.2%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.42 (95% band [-0.88, -0.08]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 16,500 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.8% (95% band 0.7% to 10.1%); rank 3 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.11, 95% band [-0.33, +0.27]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.4% (95% band 1.4% to 9.8%); rank 3 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.60 (95% band [+0.07, +1.22]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 198,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.6% (95% band 0.2% to 6.9%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.04, 95% band [-0.22, +0.30]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.5% (95% band 0.1% to 6.6%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.19, 95% band [-0.07, +0.61]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.7% (95% band 0.0% to 4.9%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.18, 95% band [-0.55, +0.06]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.0% to 5.1%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.06, 95% band [+0.00, +0.31]).

Interactions: the model has 25 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 1.7% (95% band 1.0% to 4.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.32 (95% band +1.80 to +2.56) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.35 (95% band +1.58 to +2.88) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.14 (95% band -1.81 to -0.64) when `PAY_0` = -2, -1.11 (95% band -2.00 to -0.38) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.4% to 2.8%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.25 (95% band +1.85 to +2.44) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +2.66 (95% band +2.03 to +2.79) when `PAY_AMT1` = 16,500.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 16,500: -0.47 (95% band -0.95 to -0.07) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.06 (95% band -0.57 to +0.11) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.0% to 2.3%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.22 (95% band -1.91 to -0.66) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -1.04 (95% band -1.66 to -0.66) when `PAY_AMT1` = 16,500.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 16,500: -0.54 (95% band -1.01 to -0.14) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.36 (95% band -0.77 to -0.06) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.3% to 4.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.07 (95% band +1.62 to +2.44) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.47 (95% band +2.02 to +2.76) when `BILL_AMT1` = 198,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 198,000: +0.42 (95% band +0.00 to +0.88) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.82 (95% band +0.18 to +1.49) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.0% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.21 (95% band -1.76 to -0.65) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.76 (95% band -1.84 to -0.52) when `BILL_AMT1` = 198,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 198,000: +0.36 (95% band +0.09 to +1.17) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.81 (95% band +0.07 to +1.22) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 1.5%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 16,500: -0.43 (95% band -0.82 to -0.07) when `AGE` = 23, -0.37 (95% band -0.93 to -0.07) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: -0.02 (95% band -0.23 to +0.29) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.04 (95% band -0.44 to +0.25) when `PAY_AMT1` = 16,500.
- `BILL_AMT2 & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.0% to 1.5%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 191,000: +0.23 (95% band -0.02 to +0.81) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, +0.12 (95% band -0.22 to +0.56) when `PAY_AMT3` = 17,300.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 17,300: -0.14 (95% band -0.53 to +0.10) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.25 (95% band -0.94 to +0.03) when `BILL_AMT2` = 191,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 198,000: +0.78 (95% band +0.05 to +1.19) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.57 (95% band +0.08 to +1.17) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,400: -0.09 (95% band -0.40 to +0.26) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.30 (95% band -0.41 to +0.24) when `BILL_AMT1` = 198,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 2.5%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.21 (95% band -1.86 to -0.69) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -1.09 (95% band -2.00 to -0.63) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,400: -0.12 (95% band -0.48 to +0.50) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.00 (95% band -0.33 to +0.36) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 2.2%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.16 (95% band -1.83 to -0.65) when `AGE` = 23, -1.12 (95% band -1.86 to -0.64) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.02 (95% band -0.23 to +0.27) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.06 (95% band -0.29 to +0.46) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
- 15 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 4.0%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by the applicant's most recent repayment status (PAY_0): applicants who were behind on payments by one month or more carry a much higher predicted risk, with the effect rising sharply from one month of delay to two or more months, while those who paid in full or used revolving credit carry lower risk."},{"id":2,"text":"The size of the credit limit (LIMIT_BAL) is the second most important driver: limits below 160,000 NT dollars raise predicted risk, and limits at or above that level lower it, with a net effect across the typical range of roughly -1.1 on the log-odds scale."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in the latest month (PAY_AMT1) matters less, with larger payments associated with somewhat lower predicted risk, though the shape of this effect between the low and high ends is not resolved by the data."},{"id":4,"text":"The latest bill amount (BILL_AMT1) pushes predicted risk up modestly as it rises, but this effect is uncertain, as its range of plausible values is wide."},{"id":5,"text":"The model's interactions are noticeable: the effect of repayment status is somewhat stronger when the credit limit or latest bill is high, and the effect of the credit limit is weaker for applicants who are already behind on payments, though these interaction effects are individually small and uncertain."},{"id":6,"text":"Age, the earlier bill and payment amounts, and education contribute little to the model's predictions, and the data do not settle whether their small estimated effects are real."}]}
